guard_streams.write_limit: National programme targets, definitions and intervention mechanisms are aggregate policy context and cannot establish current selected-parcel serviceability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The Project Gigabit guidance was published on 1 April 2022.
The page was last updated on 26 November 2025.
Project Gigabit targets hard-to-reach premises.
The programme states a target of gigabit coverage for 99% of premises by 2032.
More than 30 Project Gigabit contracts had been awarded.
The voucher component offers up to £4,500 for eligible premises.
Voucher support is intended outside qualifying commercial or procurement coverage.
Gigabit-capable service is defined as at least 1 Gbit/s.
The page describes superfast as over 30 Mbit/s and ultrafast as over 100 Mbit/s.
The guidance records the planned ADSL phase-out date of 31 January 2027.

guard_streams.authority: Building Digital UK / Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
guard_streams.write_limit: Process-review findings and programme outputs are evaluation evidence; they do not prove current broadband availability or measured performance for nearby selected parcels.

facts.detail: The GigaHubs Process Review was published on 26 June 2026.
Belmana and GC Insight conducted the review.
The wider evaluation runs from 2022 to 2027.
The reviewed GigaHubs programme covers 2021 to 2026.
It focuses on remote public buildings such as schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
The review is organised around two principal themes.
Evidence included programme management data and stakeholder interviews.
Six projects identified 2,554 potential sites.
Around 1,200 sites had been connected at the review point.
The review estimated around 30 surrounding premises passed per connected Hub.

guard_streams.write_limit: Operator deployment plans are forecasts and aggregate projections; exact selected-parcel availability requires current premises-level archive and orderability validation.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2026 planned-deployment report on 13 May 2026.
The report reflects operator plans as of January 2026.
The plans cover deployment over the following three years.
The report covers operator private and publicly funded deployment plans.
It does not treat public-authority aspirations as operator deployment plans.
Reported plans could take full fibre to 28.1 million premises, or 92%.
Reported plans could take gigabit-capable coverage to 29 million premises, or 95%.
High-confidence full-fibre coverage was projected at 87% in 2028 and 88% in 2029.
Planned full-fibre rural coverage rises from 66% to 86%.
Operators reported plans for about 6,950 fixed-wireless-access masts to be built or upgraded.

guard_streams.source: How to get more from your broadband
guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer guidance, estimated checker speeds and technology bands do not establish exact current serviceability or measured speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the guide on 19 July 2023.
The guide says faster or cheaper broadband may be available.
Superfast broadband is described as available to more than nine in ten homes.
The guide presents a three-step process for reviewing service options.
The coverage checker provides operators' estimated fastest available speeds.
The guide warns that actual speed may differ from estimates.
Standard broadband is described as below 30 Mbit/s.
Superfast broadband is described as 30 to 300 Mbit/s.
Ultrafast broadband is described as above 300 Mbit/s.
Options include upgrading, renegotiating, switching or retaining the current package.

guard_streams.source: Are you in or out of contract?
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract status, notification and switching guidance are consumer-process evidence, not physical broadband coverage or selected-parcel measured-speed evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the contract-status guide on 12 April 2022.
The page was last updated on 17 July 2026.
Typical minimum terms include 12, 18 or 24 months.
An early termination fee may apply during the minimum term.
Out-of-contract customers can shop around or switch.
Providers must notify customers when a contract is ending.
Out-of-contract customers receive annual best-tariff information.
End-of-contract notifications are sent 10 to 40 days before the contract ends.
Notifications may be delivered by text, email or letter.
Notifications include end date, notice requirements, prices, deals and relevant bundle dates.
